title: Pattern Strip
description: Find the group that repeats, or the move made at every step, and carry a picture pattern on until it comes round again.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit. With navDots the dots are controls in AI mode too: a tap on a dot starts that phase.

stage.sizing: the frame is min(100vw, 177.78vh) wide and min(100vh, 56.25vw) tall (dvh where supported); the svg fills it. Nothing scrolls.

bands.header: 0 to 80. One line: the tool name, a measured dot, the phase concept; Hint, sound and restart as round controls far right.
bands.canvas: 92 to 640. One rounded card holding the key at its top right (Answer, Close, Enter, Next, or the Yes / No keys; no question bar), the working area (the whole card until Answer is tapped) and the answer drawer that slides in from the right; the summary page covers it at the end.
bands.footer: 652 to 900. The mascot at the far left on its ground line, the speech bubble beside it (y 656 to 892, the question and every line, printed), one small dot per phase at the right.

zones.layout: board, key only: no question bar, only its key at the right end of the top row (the question is on the bubble); the working area is the whole card (64, 108, 1472 x 520) until the child taps Answer, when the answer drawer (as tall as the working area, the key on its top row reading Close) slides in from the right
zones.controls: circles r 28 at cx 1388, 1460, 1532, cy 40: Hint (data-control again), sound, restart; 72-unit finger boxes
zones.dots: one small dot per phase at the footer's right (72-unit finger boxes, centred on the bubble), no text; in user AND AI mode each is a button (data-control phase-dot, data-phase k) that starts its phase

stage.noSidebar: There is no sidebar. The canvas takes every unit the chrome can spare.
stage.noScoreBox: There is no score box on the stage. The score leaves on finished and onComplete and is shown once, as stars on the summary page.

writeup.why: Find the group that repeats, or the move made at every step, and carry a picture pattern on until it comes round to the start again.
writeup.look: A long strip of cells with the last few empty, a turn dial under it, and one or two big shapes whose sides are tapped to count them.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only. 'Pattern Strip' sits in ink at the far left, with a small dot set clear of the name by measuring it. The phase title sits beside the dot on the same line, then the host's navigation, and again, sound and restart stand as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at 64,108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: the places filled against the places this phase leaves empty, two numbers in ink. The first climbs by one as each cell fills, and the second is fixed at what this phase holds. Nothing in it ever counts down and nothing in it ever reads as a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at 64,202. The strip runs across the top of the working area: ten cells, each 100 by 100 with 8 between, at 64,222, reaching 1136. Each cell holds one shape, one arrow, or one dot on a plus-shaped outline, drawn at one size and never overlapping its neighbour. The bracket rides a rail under the strip, 1072 by 24 at 64,330, and is dragged to cover any run of cells. The Pattern key then lights every copy of that run along the whole strip at once, each matching copy underlined in green. A copy that does not match is left unlit, never hidden, and the one cell in it that breaks the match is ringed in reddish purple. On the third phase the strip gives way to one or two big shapes whose sides the child taps, each tapped side lighting and a running count standing under its shape. The lower band, from 414 to 720, holds the dial on the second phase. The dial is 160 across and docks under whichever empty cell is being filled, kept inside the working area's right edge, with the turn ring 72 across at its left. Each tap turns the dial's arrow one quarter turn clockwise, the way a clock's hands go, and draws that turn as a vermilion arc. The turn ring fills one quarter at a time and closes at four, when the arrow is home. Down the right of the canvas the question sits above the answer slot at 1186,250 (356 by 92), which holds what the child has given. That rectangle is the same on every phase and is never animated in or out. Under it is the pad at 1170,368 (388 by 363). The pad is a shape tray of the cells this strip uses and a turn pad of four arrows, pointing up, right, down and left. Twelve number keys three across take over wherever a count is asked for. A word pad carries this strip's own words: group, repeat, quarter turn, clockwise, sides, first and last. The footer runs 758 to 900. The voice caption sits at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling. The phase bar sits at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own, taken from its pictures. Whatever the stage hands over is deep blue: a given term, a bead, the bottom row of a tower, a plain letter, a tile already laid. The first member of a repeating group is deep blue too, and the second member, or a second kind set beside the first, is amber. The step itself is vermilion in every tool without exception: a jump arc and its label, a quarter turn, an operation sign, a key's shift. Whatever the rule makes is green: a next term, a built box, a coded or decoded letter, a copy just laid, a tick. Whatever the child is asked to notice is reddish purple: a broken box, a closed-in gap, a doubled part, a leftover counter, a line put back. The dots of dotted paper are grey and nothing else is. Every bracket, outline, rule and blank is near-black chrome. Chrome never borrows a content colour, and no content colour is ever used for chrome. Every reading survives with the colour taken away, because a thing is told by its label or its place before it is told by its colour. A blank waiting for the child is an empty outlined box, never a faded copy of its answer.
writeup.finish: The card shows the strip the child finished, its repeating group bracketed and every copy lit, and the shapes whose sides were counted.

phases.win: every copy of the group lights along the strip and the blanks fill with the matching shapes
phases.does: draws a bracket over the group they think repeats, watches its copies light, then fills the blanks
phases.goal: the smallest group that repeats fills every blank in a row
phases.says: Which shapes come round again? Put a bracket over them.
phases.check: Away from the screen: make a row of three kinds of thing on your desk. Ask a friend to find the group.
phases.feels: the row is one group laid down again and again, and a blank is only the next place in the group
phases.hands: Before the tool is opened, make a row on a desk with real things: square, square, circle, square, square, circle, in paper cut-outs, caps or beads. Ask for the smallest group that repeats, not for the next thing. Every row of the recap's matching question takes turns between two shapes, so give a group of three early, where copying two places back goes wrong. Let the class find where it breaks, and then ask how a group could be checked without filling any blank at all.
phases.tries: A miss is answered three ways at once and none of them is the answer. First rung, from the item's own miss line: which cells come round again? Second rung, the phase's: does every copy of your group match? Third rung: the strip is cut to two whole copies of the group and one blank, and the child brackets again. The shape tray stays open behind all three rungs.

wrong.why: every row of the recap's matching question takes turns between two shapes, so copying two places back has been right four times running.
wrong.move: copies the cell two places back into every blank, which works while two shapes take turns and finds no group at all.
wrong.screen: the child's shapes stay in the blanks, and a bracket is drawn over the two cells they were copied from. The Pattern key runs that pair along the strip. On a group of three the copies stop matching at the third cell, which is left unlit and ringed in reddish purple. A bracket over three cells is then offered beside it, and every copy of that one lights.

wrong.why: a longer bracket seems safer, because it holds more of the row inside it.
wrong.move: brackets a run one cell too long, taking in the start of the next copy, and fills the blank from it.
wrong.screen: the Pattern key runs the long bracket along the strip, and each copy drifts one cell further until one does not match. That copy is left unlit with its breaking cell ringed. The child's bracket stays drawn, and it is then shortened one cell at a time, with the copies lit again after each.

phases.screen: a strip of shapes with its last two cells empty and the bracket waiting
phases.soWhat: Find the smallest group that repeats, and every blank takes the cell one whole group before it.

phases.win: the arrow settles and the turn ring closes when four quarter turns bring it home
phases.does: turns the dial until the new arrow repeats the move between the cells before it
phases.goal: the same quarter turn is made at every step, and four of them make a full turn
phases.says: How far did it turn each time? Make the same turn again.
phases.check: Point an arrow up and turn it a quarter turn clockwise three times. Which way does it point now?
phases.feels: the same small turn every time, and after four of them the arrow is back where it began
phases.hands: Give each pair a paper arrow and lay it flat on the desk pointing left. Turn it a quarter turn the way a clock's hands go, and say the new direction aloud. Keep turning and counting until the arrow comes home. Then ask how many turns brought it home, and which way it will point after eight turns, before anyone turns it.
phases.tries: First rung, from the item: how far did the arrow turn between the last two cells? Second rung, the phase's: which way do a clock's hands go? Third rung: the row is cut to two arrows one quarter turn apart, and the child makes the same turn once. The turn pad stays open.

wrong.why: a quarter turn is the same size either way, and the row shows only where the arrow pointed, not which way it moved between cells.
wrong.move: turns the arrow against a clock's hands, so a row that went up, right, down is carried on the other way round.
wrong.screen: the dial replays the move between the last two cells one quarter at a time, drawing it as a vermilion arc the way a clock's hands go. The child's arrow stays in its cell with its own arc drawn beside it, running the other way. The two arcs stand together, and nothing is marked.

wrong.why: a half turn is the easiest turn to see, because the arrow ends up pointing straight back the way it came.
wrong.move: makes a half turn at every step, so up is followed by down and the arrow never points right or left.
wrong.screen: the turn ring shows the child's move as two quarters filled, where the row made one. The dial then turns from the last cell one quarter at a time, and the arrow lands on a direction the child's row skipped. The child's arrow and the dial's stand side by side.

phases.screen: a row of arrows, each pointing a different way, with the dial under the first empty cell
phases.soWhat: A turning pattern makes the same quarter turn at every step, and four quarter turns make a full turn.
phases.concept: A quarter turn at every step

phases.win: the next shape lands with its sides lit one by one and its count under it
phases.does: taps each side of the shapes to count them, then answers the next shape or how many sides it has
phases.goal: a row can lose one side at each step and then start again from its first shape
phases.says: Count the sides of each one. What happens after three?
phases.check: A row starts with a shape of five sides and loses one each step. Name the shapes until it starts again.
phases.feels: each tapped side lights and the count climbs by one, and the next shape has one side fewer until three, when the row starts over
phases.hands: Draw a hexagon, a pentagon, a square and a triangle on the board, and count the sides of each aloud with the class. Ask what shape would have two sides, and let someone try to draw one that closes. Then ask where the row must go after the triangle. Write the side counts under the shapes, so the class sees a list of numbers that starts again.
phases.tries: First rung, from the item: tap each side of the shape and count it. Second rung, the phase's: can a closed shape with straight sides have fewer than three? Third rung: the sides of the shown shapes are counted one by one, then the next shape comes with its sides counted.

wrong.why: the shape in front has just been counted, so its own count seems to be the answer.
wrong.move: answers the count of the shown shape, and not one side fewer.
wrong.screen: the sides of the shown shape light one by one with the count climbing under it, then the next shape comes with one side fewer, each side lit and counted. The child's answer stays in the slot, unmarked.

wrong.why: every step so far has been one side fewer, so a jump back up to the first count looks like the rule being broken.
wrong.move: carries on losing sides after the triangle, and answers two.
wrong.screen: the sides of the shown shapes are counted one by one, then the next shape comes with its sides counted, and after the triangle the row's first shape comes again with its count starting over. The child's answer stays in the slot.

phases.screen: one or two big shapes with their sides ready to tap, and an empty box where the next shape comes
phases.soWhat: A row can lose one side at each step until the triangle, and then it starts again from its first shape.
phases.concept: One side fewer, then start again

writeup.delight: The third phase, when the next shape lands. Its sides light one after another with the count climbing under it, so the child sees the new shape has one side fewer than the one before, and any shown shape's sides can be tapped again to count them once more. Nothing is marked either way, and the voice says nothing at all while it happens.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with nothing in front of it. On the first phase a strip of shapes stands with its last two cells empty and the bracket parked at its left hand end. On the second a row of arrows stands, each pointing a different way, with the dial docked under the first empty cell and its turn ring open. On the third one or two big shapes stand with their sides ready to tap, and an empty box waits for the next shape. The running count at the top left holds the places filled against the places this phase leaves empty, and the answer slot and the pad stand empty down the right. One thing moves, once: the parked bracket, or the dial, or the empty cell, or the first side to tap, gives one slow pulse while the voice asks what comes round again. That pulse is the only invitation, and a finger on it is the whole way in.
writeup.freePlay: One shape of three to six sides, every side open to tap and count, and a key that brings the next shape. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer.
writeup.practice: Nine items over the three phases, easy first, on the group that repeats, a quarter turn at every step, and a row that loses a side and starts again.
voiceLines: A strip of shapes, and some cells still empty. Find what comes round again.
Which shapes come round again? Put a bracket over them.
How far did it turn each time? Make the same turn again.
Count the sides of each one. What happens after three?
Another row. Find the rule before you fill anything.
Free play. Tap each side of a shape and count them.
Look again at what stays the same from one cell to the next.
Every row carried on, and every side counted.

observations.why: A group one cell too long or too short does not start again at the same place each time, so its copies drift.
observations.soWhat: The group that repeats is found by testing it along the whole row, not by looking at the last two cells.
observations.observe: The copies lit all along the strip only when the bracket covered the smallest group that repeats.

observations.why: Each quarter turn points the arrow a new way, and there are only four ways for it to point.
observations.soWhat: A turning pattern repeats every four steps, so a far step is found by counting in fours.
observations.observe: Four quarter turns closed the ring and brought the arrow back to where it began.

observations.why: A closed shape with straight sides needs at least three, so the row cannot lose another side.
observations.soWhat: Starting again is part of the pattern, so the group runs from the first shape to the triangle.
observations.observe: The side counts went down to three and then went back to the first count.

phases.screen: a strip of shapes with its last two cells empty and the bracket waiting
phases.win: every copy of the group lights along the strip and the blanks fill with the matching shapes
phases.traceback: The smallest group is bracketed, every copy of it lights along the strip, and the blanks fill with the box one whole group before.
ladder: Bracket the beads that come round again.
Say the shapes in a row, and see where it starts over.
A shape can show up twice inside one group.
Does every copy of your group match?
Bracket until the same shapes come round in the same order.

phases.screen: a row of arrows, each pointing a different way, with the dial under the first empty cell
phases.win: the arrow settles and the turn ring closes when four quarter turns bring it home
phases.traceback: The dial replays the quarter turn from the last arrow, the way a clock's hands go, and the row fills with the arrows that turn makes.
ladder: Press Turn to see the move between the two arrows.
Follow the dot with your finger, the way a clock goes.
How many quarter turns make one full turn?
Which way do a clock's hands go?
Four quarter turns bring the arrow home, so count in fours.

phases.screen: one or two big shapes with their sides ready to tap, and an empty box where the next shape comes
phases.win: the next shape lands with its sides lit one by one and its count under it
phases.traceback: The sides of the shown shapes are counted one by one, then the next shape comes with its sides counted.
ladder: Tap each side of the shape to count, then take one away.
Read the side counts along the row, one at a time.
Tap each side, and see how the counts change.
Can a closed shape with straight sides have fewer than three?
Say the side counts out loud, and listen for the jump.

items.win: Yes, red comes first and blue second.
Yes, the star and moon take turns.
Yes, square, square, circle comes round.
Yes, each arrow is one quarter further round.
Yes, one more quarter turn puts it there.
Yes, two full turns bring it back round.
Yes, one side fewer makes five sides.
Yes, the counts start over after three.
Yes, the climb ends on five sides.

onWrong.marks: Nothing is marked, nothing resets, no colour means good or bad. The child's answer stays; the pad re-opens after the traceback.
tracebacks: Phase 1: The smallest group is bracketed, every copy of it lights along the strip, and the blanks fill with the box one whole group before.
Phase 2: The dial replays the quarter turn from the last arrow, the way a clock's hands go, and the row fills with the arrows that turn makes.
Phase 3: The sides of the shown shapes are counted one by one, then the next shape comes with its sides counted.

voice.opening: A strip of shapes, and some cells still empty. Find what comes round again.
voice.onFreePlay: Free play. Tap each side of a shape and count them.
voice.onMiss: the item's own miss line, then the phase's two ladder rungs, shown at once UNDER the pinned instruction and kept until the child acts again
voice.onFinish: Every row carried on, and every side counted.
voice.rules: Silent: nothing is spoken (no device speech, no recorded clips, no Tap to start cover). The speech bubble is the guide: every instruction and hint is one printed page, numbers as words. The lesson is action-driven in every mode: a guide step's instruction stays until the child does the act it names; a wrong act shows that step's hint under the pinned instruction, a wrong answer the next rung of its ladder, and the hint stays unchanged until the child acts again; a right answer's next question, a phase's next phase and the summary's rows follow by themselves after a short celebration. The header's Hint key shows the step's hint or the next rung on demand. What is heard is sound effects (Web Audio), switched by the sound button, on in every mode. In classroom mode nothing waits for a tap except the pieces of a long line (the blinking arrow; a tap, Enter, Space, ArrowRight or PageDown on the bubble shows the next piece), and a tap on the bubble when nothing waits is the teacher's skip.

guide.playsOn: guide steps on phase 1, 2, 3: the phase opens on its first instruction and waits for the child's act (getState guideStep, guideSteps, guideOn); the agent's check() performs the current step; the last act opens the first question. Other phases open on their printed teach lines, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

toolQuestions.source: props.questions ?? props.additionalProps?.questions is read; the authored rows below keep their stage (fitHost returns null).

items.planQuestion: A bead string goes red, blue, blue, red, blue, blue, and then two empty places. Which beads go in the two places?

question.en: Which beads go in the two boxes?

items.planQuestion: Star, moon, star, moon, star, and then an empty place. What goes in the empty place?

question.en: What goes in the empty box?

items.planAnswer: Moon, because star and moon take turns

items.planQuestion: Square, square, circle, square, square, circle, square, and then an empty place. What goes there, and what is the group that repeats?

question.en: What goes there, and what is the group that repeats?

items.planAnswer: Square, and the group is square, square, circle

items.planQuestion: An arrow points left. At every step it makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does it point after one, two, three and four steps?

question.en: It makes a quarter turn clockwise each step: which way after each of four steps?

items.planAnswer: Up, then right, then down, then left again

items.planQuestion: A dot sits at the bottom of a plus shape, then at the left, then at the top. It moves one place round clockwise each time. Where does it sit next?

question.en: The dot goes to the next arm of the plus, clockwise: where does it end up?

items.planQuestion: An arrow points down and makes a quarter turn clockwise at every step. Which way does it point after eight steps?

question.en: After eight more quarter turns clockwise, which way does the arrow point?

items.planAnswer: Down again, because four quarter turns make a full turn and eight make two full turns

items.planQuestion: A row starts with a seven-sided shape and loses one side at every step. How many shapes are in the row before it has to start again?

question.en: The row loses one side each step: how many sides will the next shape have?

items.planAnswer: Five: seven sides, six, five, four and three. A closed shape with straight sides needs at least three, so the row then starts again

items.planQuestion: A row goes pentagon, square, triangle, pentagon, square, and then an empty place. Which shape goes there, and which comes after it?

question.en: How many sides do the shapes in the two empty boxes have?

items.planAnswer: A triangle, and then a pentagon again

items.planQuestion: A row goes triangle, square, pentagon, triangle, square, and then an empty place. What goes in the empty place?

question.en: What shape goes in the empty box of this row?

items.planAnswer: A pentagon, because the shapes gain one side each time, three, four, five, and then start again at three

scoring.wrong: costs nothing, never marked, counted only for first try accuracy
scoring.stars: one for finishing, two at sixty per cent right first time, three at ninety; hidden with the first-try line by showScore false
scoring.phaseMount: a mount scores every phase it plays, from its phase to the last (+5 a question; phases of 3, 3, 3 questions)
scoring.finishCard: stars and the Right first time line under the phase rows on the summary page

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 3 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once. Present: rounded and clamped to one to 3 (a phase asked for above 3 opens phase 3, the last); the tool starts at that phase and, as the NCERT tools do, walks on by itself after each phase's last question (its closing line, then 1.4 s), in user and AI mode alike, through phase 3 to the summary page (a tool with nextKey, runtime r48+: in user mode it waits for the child's blinking Next key instead, after every question and every phase, and the last phase's key opens the summary; AI mode, and a host that mounts one phase without navigableDots, walk on by themselves); finished once, from the summary page.
hostContract.navigableDots: true (or no phase): user mode, the phase dots are controls; otherwise AI mode, the dots show progress and the agent drives window.toolApi.

onProgress.done: questions right so far in this phase

hostContract.emits: every event is dispatched on window and, when framed, posted to window.parent as { type: 'event', name, detail }

phases.concept: A quarter turn at every step
One side fewer, then start again

terminalEvent.name: finished
terminalEvent.fires: once per mount, from the summary page after the last phase, 5 s after the page opens (its lines may still be going on); one-shot guarded and re-armed by restart or Play again; never sent at the end of an earlier phase (the tool walks on), and never if Free play or Play again is tapped first
